title: Stream Error View
description: Payload of the view:stream_error bridge message — the Stream Presenter's StreamErrorView, serialized across the CEF bridge so the UI can show the producer what went wrong (Requirement 23.2). Covers stream:error and all seven error:* envelope types, which requirement 5.5 routes to the same place. The error:* types have no bundled payload schema at all, which is why this document matters more than it looks: it is the only schema describing what the UI receives for them, and without it the TypeScript side would be typed from whatever the C++ happened to send.

code.description: Machine-readable error code, as the server sent it. Stable enough for the UI to branch on and to key a translation off, which is what it should do rather than translating the message below.

message.description: Producer-safe explanation, as the server sent it. stream-error.schema.json documents it as safe to display. English, from the server, so the UI prefers a translation keyed on code and falls back to this.

envelopeType.description: The envelope type that triggered the error, when the error answers one. Empty when it does not — an error:* type reporting a condition rather than refusing a message.

validationErrors.description: Rendered schema validation failures, when that was the cause (Requirement 4.1). Already a single formatted string rather than a structured list: the extension's validator produces prose, and the UI shows it for diagnosis rather than branching on it. Empty when the error was not a validation failure.

$comment: Only the last stream error is carried, not a list — the presenter holds one. A second error replaces the first, which is the right shape for a banner and the wrong one for a history; nothing in requirements 16 or 23 asks for a history.
